newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ says no meeting soon on Australia beyond rights.
newsitem.headline: NZ says no meeting soon on Australia beyond rights.

text.p: Transport Minister Maurice Williamson has failed to win cabinet backing for an early meeting to press New Zealand's case for aviation "beyond rights" with Australia at ministerial level, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
Williamson sought cabinet approval on Monday to continue negotiating with the Australian government, but the spokesman said it was decided not to send him.

"The prime minister (Jim Bolger) and cabinet feel there is no point in talking now. The consensus was: what's the point?'" the spokesman said, referring to Canberra's apparent reluctance to negotiate until the shape of the New Zealand government was clear.
New Zealand has a caretaker National Party conservative government following an inconclusive general election last month.
Australian Transport Minister John Sharp was quoted last week as saying his government would be prepared to negotiate "as soon as we have someone to negotiate with".
However, he also said Air New Zealand's recent provided greater flexibility and more options in tackling the beyond rights issue.

Last Friday Williamson said an agreement extending Air New Zealand's rights to fly through Australia to other destinations could be finalised later this month if New Zealand political parties agreed to pursue a deal.
He said there was a transport ministers conference in Australia on November 15 where he could meet Sharp to try to conclude an agreement.
The government spokesman said officials were still talking over the whole issue of beyond-rights. "We are moving pieces but not making progress," he said.

A trans-Tasman single aviation market accord, which came into force last Friday, allows Australian and New Zealand companies to fly within and between both countries without restriction, but there are still limits on flying across the Tasman and on to a third destination.
Williamson said last week the beyond rights aspect of the single aviation market agreement had been almost finalised about a week before last month's general election.
However it was not considered appropriate for governments to conclude major agreements so close to an election, so the deal was put on hold.

Both the caretaker conservative National government and the main opposition Labour party are negotiating with New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, over the shape of the next government.
Labour foreign affairs spokesman Mike Moore has criticised Williamson for "gross failure" in not advancing New Zealand's case.
"At the very minimum his office should advise Mr Sharp that the New Zealand case stands unchanged and we still desire this agreement," Mooore said in a statement.
